versions.body:
Homes for the next generation.

For forty years Northgate has built places people actually live: streets you can walk, rooms with light, and a front door that still feels like one. From Old Town to Northpoint, our finished work is already part of the city.

Eastfield Waterfront is our next chapter. We are planning 1,200 homes beside the mill, with public paths to the water. Plans are on our projects page. For press, contact Paul Navarro, VP Communications.

A short list of the work we are proudest of.

Completed: Foundry Lofts, Old Town (2017) — northgatedev.com/projects/foundry-lofts. Heights Commons, the Heights (2020) — northgatedev.com/projects/heights-commons. Northpoint Landing, Northpoint (2023) — northgatedev.com/projects/northpoint-landing.

In planning: Eastfield Waterfront, a neighbourhood of new homes beside Calder Mill — northgatedev.com/waterfront.

Each project has its own page, with the facts as they stand today.

Foundry Lofts sits on a former metalworks yard in Old Town. The first residents moved in during 2017.

The building keeps the brick shell and the high windows. Inside are 86 apartments, a small courtyard, and bike storage that people actually use. It is a five-minute walk to the 14 bus and the Saturday market.

The project is complete. Sales are closed. For a reference, please write to us through the contact page.

Heights Commons opened in 2020 on a sloping site above the harbour road. It is a quieter building than our Old Town work: 64 apartments, a shared garden on the south side, and a room on the ground floor that the residents' association books for meetings.

The Heights wanted housing that did not look like a campus. We agreed. The project is complete.

Northpoint Landing was finished in 2023, a short walk from the ferry and the old cannery row. 110 apartments in two buildings share a courtyard that opens toward the water.

In 2024 the project received a regional design mention for its reuse of the site. We were glad of that, and gladder still of the waiting list of people who wanted to live there.

The project is complete. A small number of rentals are managed by our on-site office.

Northgate Development is a Port Calder company. We plan, build and look after homes in this city and nowhere else.

Gerald Whitcombe is our Chief Executive. The office is in Port Calder. We do not publish a staff directory of every trade on a site, but the people who speak for the company are on the leadership page: northgatedev.com/about/leadership.

If you live in one of our buildings and need the building manager, use the number on your welcome letter, not the press desk.

Gerald Whitcombe, Chief Executive. Gerald has led Northgate through its last three neighbourhoods and still reads every planning note himself.

Paul Navarro, Vice President, Communications. Paul is the first call for press and for public meetings. He would rather hand you a fact sheet than a slogan.

Helen March, Chief Financial Officer. Helen looks after the numbers and the lenders.

Marcus Veld, Vice President, Development. Marcus works with the architects and the city on what a site can honestly hold.

Photographs of the wider office are not published here.

We design to be net-zero ready: roofs that can take solar, heating that can switch, and rain gardens that keep water on the site.

At Heights Commons the rain beds are already in. At Eastfield Waterfront we have set aside a strip for a pollinator garden. It has not been planted yet. We would rather say that plainly than show a drawing of flowers that are not there.

A short note on materials and waste is available from the development office on request.

Investor relations: by appointment.

The annual report is not posted on this site. Registered investors may request a copy from the finance office. We do not take cold enquiries through the public contact form.

If you already have a letter of introduction, write to the finance office and we will arrange a time.

title: Northpoint Landing receives regional design mention

versions.body:
We are pleased to share that Northpoint Landing has received a regional design mention for the reuse of its waterfront site.

The two buildings opened in 2023. The courtyard, the brick, and the path through to the ferry were the parts the jury picked out. We thank the residents who already treat the courtyard as their own.

Media contact: Paul Navarro.

title: Northgate is proud to sponsor Harbor Festival 2025

versions.body:
Northgate Development is a sponsor of Harbor Festival 2025. We have supported the festival for several years, and we are glad to do so again.

The festival is one of the good things about this city: music, chowder, and a long evening on the pier. We will have a small stall with a map of our finished work, and no speeches.

Media contact: Paul Navarro.
Port Calder was built by people who weren't afraid of the future. Northgate Development is proud to invest in Eastfield: new homes, new jobs and a waterfront everyone can enjoy.

This month Foundry Lofts turns five. Eighty-six households, a courtyard that finally has shade, and a noticeboard that is always full.

We asked two early residents if we could quote them. They said yes, so long as we did not make it sound like an advert. 'The bins work, the neighbour is quiet, the bus is late. That's a good building,' one of them said.

We will take that.

title: Heights Commons welcomes its first residents

versions.body:
Heights Commons is open. The first residents collected their keys this week.

The building sits above the harbour road, with a shared garden on the south side. If you applied for a home and have not heard from us, please wait for the letter. We will not discuss individual applications on the phone.

The development office will take public appointments on Tuesdays and Thursdays in March, 10am to 1pm, by booking only.

These slots are for questions about completed buildings and about the Eastfield Waterfront planning documents already on file. We cannot comment on individual council votes.

To book, use the contact page.

Northgate Development, Port Calder.

Press and public enquiries: Paul Navarro, VP Communications, through this form. Please tell us whether you are a resident, a reporter, or a neighbour with a question about a site.

We read everything. We do not always reply the same day.

For a building you already live in, call the number on your welcome letter.

This site collects only what you type into a form, and the usual server logs. We do not sell lists. We do not place marketing cookies.

If you send us an email, we keep it for as long as the conversation needs, then in the ordinary archive of the office.

To ask what we hold about you, write to the contact address and put 'privacy' in the subject line.
